newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel mixed, jet fuel falls.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel mixed, jet fuel falls.

text.p: The gas oil market was mixed with physical barrels being traded higher, while swaps slipped on concerns over slow regional demand, traders said on Tuesday.
They said jet fuel continued to slide amid a lack of buying interest.
They said the gas oil swaps market was nervous about how long a local trader, who has been supporting the market since early March, could sustain his presence.
"The paper market reflect what the fundamental is," one trader said.

"But the local trader is pushing the (physical) market up. How long can the man continue to support the market? If he can continue to support, the paper can come up to meet the physical levels, if not the physical will fall to meet paper values which will in turn go down even further."
The trader on Tuesday bought another 300,000 barrels of gas oil, bringing their total to about 5.4 million barrels and helped to boost the physical market.
They said a European major sold an early April cargo of gas oil at $29.00 per barrel fob to a Japanese trader, which was 40-50 cents above the deals done on Monday.
A Dutch trader sold 150,000 barrels to the local trader for April 16-20 lifting at $28.20 a barrel, 20 cents over the cargo bought on Monday.
At current high prices, sellers have "to forget about China, its history" one trader said. China is only interested to buy at $205 on a cost-and-freight basis, traders said.

Jet fuel was offered twice at lower levels of $26.80 for April 15-19 and April 20-24. Lack of regional demand saw buyers staying away. Traders said Indonesia was expected to buy less in April compared with February and March.
Nepal has issued a tender to buy gas oil and kerosene for May deliveries, which closes on April 1.
Swaps gas oil lost 25 cents per barrel from Monday to be last quoted at $26.65/$26.75 for April.
